criteria.evidence: Entry uses ### Added, ### Changed, ### Security, ### Fixed, ### Housekeeping, ### Thanks, matching existing entries.
Every bullet ends with one or more `[#NNNN](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/NNNN)` links.
Replay cites the same 37 unique PRs as the reference (1926, 2119, 2140, 2142, 2151–2158, 2163, 2169–2174, 2178–2233 set); turn 0 says it covered all merged PRs since 0.10.3.
Thanks section credits @ChetanReddyC, @MuskanPaliwal, @Solarthis; turn 0 explains the fork-branch-provenance method used to classify external contributors.
Security bullets such as 'OAuth token exchange now refuses to follow a redirect to a different host' state only the change and condition, no attack scenarios.
Turn 1 removed 'malicious', 'could have', 'silent code execution' framing; final Security bullets are plainly worded.
Turn 2: 'Trimmed every bullet ... down to one short, neutral sentence'; final bullets are ~100–200 chars versus the multi-sentence draft style.

judge.reason: The replay produced a complete 0.10.4 entry with the correct placement, headings, PR links, the same 37-PR coverage as the reference, and a Thanks section with stated contributor-classification reasoning. Security bullets are neutral and change-only, and all bullets were shortened to single sentences in the final pass; the pre-turn-2 draft is not directly observable, which is the main source of doubt.
